notes: items apply nationally; regions[P].items apply to the home province (province of incorporation, or of the registered office for federal corporations, or of operation for unincorporated businesses); extraProvincialItems apply to each other province where a corporation carries on business (and to the home province of a federal corporation); operatingItems apply to every province where the business operates; employerItems apply where employees work. The three territories are covered the same way.

items.name: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
items.rule: Within 6 months after financial year end
items.applies: Every corporation resident in Canada, including inactive corporations
items.description: The federal corporate income tax return; provincial corporate tax for every province except Quebec and Alberta is calculated and filed on the T2 as well. Late filing costs 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% a month.

items.name: Corporate Income Tax Balance Payment
items.rule: 2 months after financial year end (3 months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations)
items.applies: Corporations with tax owing for the year
items.description: The balance of federal and provincial corporate tax is due before the T2 itself; interest runs from the balance-due date.

items.name: Corporate Tax Instalments
items.rule: Monthly, by the last day of each month of the financial year (quarterly for eligible small CCPCs)
items.applies: Corporations whose tax payable was more than $3,000 in the current or previous year
items.description: Instalments are based on the prior years' tax; small Canadian-controlled private corporations that qualify may pay quarterly instead.

items.name: CBCA Annual Return (with Individuals with Significant Control)
items.rule: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation (none in the year of incorporation)
items.description: Filed online with Corporations Canada, confirming directors, addresses and the individuals with significant control; missing it for a year risks dissolution.
items.authority: Corporations Canada (ISED), Canada Business Corporations Act

items.name: Notify Corporations Canada of Changes (directors, office, significant control)
items.rule: Within 15 days of the change
items.description: Changes of directors or registered office address, and changes to the individuals with significant control, must be filed with Corporations Canada within 15 days; the ISC register must be updated as well.

items.name: Individuals with Significant Control Register — Annual Review
items.rule: At least once each financial year
items.description: Corporations must keep a register of individuals with significant control and take reasonable steps to update it at least once a year.

items.name: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and Financial Statements
items.rule: Within 6 months after financial year end (and no more than 15 months after the last meeting)
items.applies: Corporations (a written resolution signed by all shareholders can replace the meeting)
items.description: Directors place the annual financial statements before the shareholders; shareholders may consent in writing to waive an audit where the law allows.
items.authority: Canada Business Corporations Act / provincial Business Corporations Acts

items.name: T5 Slips and Summary (dividends paid)
items.rule: Last day of February (for the previous calendar year)
items.applies: Corporations that paid dividends or interest to residents
items.description: Dividends paid to Canadian-resident shareholders are reported on T5 slips.

items.name: T1 Income Tax Return with Business Income (Form T2125)
items.rule: 15 June (balance of tax still due 30 April)
items.description: Self-employed individuals file by 15 June, but any tax owing is due 30 April and interest runs from then.

items.name: Personal Tax Balance Payment
items.rule: 30 April
items.description: The balance of personal income tax for the previous year is due 30 April even though the self-employed return itself is due 15 June.

items.name: Personal Tax Instalments
items.rule: 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December
items.applies: Individuals whose net tax owing exceeded $3,000 ($1,800 in Quebec) in the current and one of the two previous years
items.description: The CRA sends instalment reminders showing the suggested amounts.

items.name: T5013 Partnership Information Return
items.rule: 31 March if all partners are individuals (5 months after year end if any partner is a corporation)
items.applies: Partnerships with more than $2 million of revenue plus expenses or $5 million of assets, or with a corporate or trust partner
items.description: Reports the partnership's income and each partner's share on T5013 slips.

items.name: GST/HST Registration
items.rule: Once taxable sales exceed $30,000 in a single quarter or over four consecutive quarters
items.applies: Businesses not yet registered for GST/HST
items.description: Small suppliers under $30,000 may register voluntarily; once over the threshold you must register and start charging GST/HST.

items.name: GST/HST Return (annual filer)
items.rule: 3 months after financial year end (individuals with business income: 15 June, with payment by 30 April)
items.applies: GST/HST registrants with annual reporting periods
items.description: Annual filers with net tax of $3,000 or more for the previous year also pay quarterly instalments.

items.name: GST/HST Return (quarterly filer)
items.rule: 1 month after the end of each quarter of the financial year
items.applies: GST/HST registrants with quarterly reporting periods
items.description: Returns and payment are due one month after each reporting period; filing electronically is mandatory for most registrants.

items.name: GST/HST Return (monthly filer)
items.rule: 1 month after the end of each month
items.applies: GST/HST registrants with monthly reporting periods (required over $6 million of sales)
items.description: Each month's return and payment are due by the end of the following month.

items.name: Payroll Program Account (RP) Registration
items.rule: Before the first payroll remittance is due
items.description: Open a CRA payroll account before paying employees; deduct CPP, EI and income tax from every pay.

items.name: Payroll Source Deductions Remittance (CPP, EI, income tax)
items.rule: By the 15th of the month after the pay date (regular remitters; larger employers remit more often)
items.description: Employee deductions plus the employer's CPP and EI share are remitted to the CRA; outside Quebec provincial income tax is included.

items.name: T4 Slips and Summary
items.rule: Last day of February (for the previous calendar year)
items.description: Each employee receives a T4 slip, and the T4 summary reconciles the year's remittances.

items.name: Record of Employment (ROE)
items.rule: Within 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period in which an employee's earnings are interrupted
items.description: Issued electronically to Service Canada whenever an employee stops working (leaves, is laid off, or goes on leave).

items.name: T106 Information Return (transactions with non-resident related parties)
items.rule: With the T2, within 6 months after financial year end
items.applies: Corporations whose reportable transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents exceed $1 million in the year
items.description: Discloses each non-resident related party and the transactions with it; penalties apply per slip for late filing.

items.name: Contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Documentation (s.247)
items.rule: In place by the T2 filing due date
items.description: Documentation supporting arm's-length pricing must exist by the filing due date and be provided within 3 months of a CRA request, or a 10% transfer pricing penalty can apply.

items.name: Non-Resident Withholding (Part XIII) and NR4 Return
items.rule: Withholding remitted by the 15th of the month after payment; NR4 slips and summary by 31 March
items.applies: Corporations paying dividends, interest, rent or management fees to a non-resident parent or other non-residents
items.description: Withholding tax of 25% (reduced by tax treaty) applies to many payments to non-residents; each year's payments are reported on NR4 slips.

items.name: Ontario Annual Return
items.rule: Within 6 months after financial year end
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

items.name: Ontario Business Name Registration Renewal
items.rule: Every 5 years from registration (renewable up to 6 months early)
items.applies: Sole proprietors and partnerships operating under a name other than the owners' own names
items.description: Registrations under the Business Names Act expire after 5 years; set the renewal date from the registration certificate.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Ontario
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Ontario
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Ontario carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: Corporations from other Canadian jurisdictions file an initial return under the Corporations Information Act within 60 days of starting business in Ontario; federal and other-province corporations do not file Ontario annual returns.

employerItems.name: Ontario Employer Health Tax (EHT) Annual Return
employerItems.rule: 15 March (monthly instalments by the 15th if Ontario payroll exceeds $5 million)
employerItems.applies: Employers whose total Ontario payroll exceeds the $1 million exemption
employerItems.description: Eligible employers are exempt on the first $1 million of Ontario remuneration; employers above it file an annual return.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB))
employerItems.rule: Premiums monthly or quarterly as assigned; annual reconciliation by 31 March
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Ontario (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) when you hire in Ontario, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

items.name: BC Annual Report
items.rule: Within 2 months after each anniversary of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in British Columbia
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in British Columbia
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside British Columbia carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in British Columbia and appoints an attorney for service where required.

extraProvincialItems.name: British Columbia Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: Within 2 months after each anniversary of registration in BC (we use the incorporation date; change it if the registration date differs)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside British Columbia registered there (not corporations from Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, under the New West Partnership)
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the British Columbia registry each year to stay in good standing.

employerItems.name: BC Employer Health Tax (EHT) Return
employerItems.rule: 31 March (instalments on 15 June, 15 September and 15 December for larger payrolls)
employerItems.applies: Employers whose BC payroll exceeds the $1 million exemption
employerItems.description: Employers register once BC remuneration exceeds $1 million in a calendar year.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (WorkSafeBC)
employerItems.rule: Quarterly reporters: payroll and premiums by 20 April, 20 July, 20 October and 20 January; annual reporters: Annual Payroll Report by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in British Columbia (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with WorkSafeBC when you hire in British Columbia, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

operatingItems.name: BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) Return
operatingItems.rule: By the last day of the month after each reporting period (monthly, quarterly or annual, as assigned)
operatingItems.applies: Businesses registered to collect BC PST
operatingItems.description: Businesses selling taxable goods or services in BC register for PST separately from GST.

items.name: Alberta Annual Return
items.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Alberta
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Alberta
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Alberta carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in Alberta and appoints an attorney for service where required.

extraProvincialItems.name: Alberta Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of registration in Alberta (we use the incorporation date; change it if the registration date differs)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Alberta registered there (not corporations from British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, under the New West Partnership)
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the Alberta registry each year to stay in good standing.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (WCB-Alberta)
employerItems.rule: Annual return of insurable earnings by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Alberta (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with WCB-Alberta when you hire in Alberta, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

operatingItems.name: Alberta Corporate Income Tax Return (AT1)
operatingItems.rule: Within 6 months after financial year end
operatingItems.applies: Corporations with a permanent establishment in Alberta
operatingItems.description: Alberta administers its own corporate income tax, so an AT1 is filed with Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration as well as the federal T2.

items.name: Saskatchewan Annual Return
items.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Saskatchewan
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Saskatchewan
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Saskatchewan carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in Saskatchewan and appoints an attorney for service where required.

extraProvincialItems.name: Saskatchewan Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of registration in Saskatchewan (we use the incorporation date; change it if the registration date differs)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Saskatchewan registered there (not corporations from British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, under the New West Partnership)
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the Saskatchewan registry each year to stay in good standing.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (Saskatchewan Workers' Compensation Board)
employerItems.rule: Employer's Payroll Statement by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Saskatchewan (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with Saskatchewan Workers' Compensation Board when you hire in Saskatchewan, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

operatingItems.name: Saskatchewan Provincial Sales Tax (PST) Return
operatingItems.rule: By the last day of the month after each reporting period when filed and paid electronically (the 20th for paper returns)
operatingItems.applies: Businesses registered to collect Saskatchewan PST
operatingItems.description: Saskatchewan PST is reported to the Ministry of Finance separately from GST.

items.name: Manitoba Annual Return
items.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Manitoba
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Manitoba
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Manitoba carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in Manitoba and appoints an attorney for service where required.

extraProvincialItems.name: Manitoba Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of registration in Manitoba (we use the incorporation date; change it if the registration date differs)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Manitoba registered there (not corporations from British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, under the New West Partnership)
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the Manitoba registry each year to stay in good standing.

employerItems.name: Manitoba Health and Post-Secondary Education Tax Levy
employerItems.rule: Monthly return and payment by the 15th of the following month
employerItems.applies: Employers whose Manitoba payroll exceeds the $2.5 million exemption (2026)
employerItems.description: The payroll levy applies above the annual exemption, at a reduced rate up to $5 million of payroll.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (WCB Manitoba)
employerItems.rule: Annual payroll report by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Manitoba (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with WCB Manitoba when you hire in Manitoba, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

operatingItems.name: Manitoba Retail Sales Tax (RST) Return
operatingItems.rule: By the 20th of the month after each reporting period
operatingItems.applies: Businesses registered to collect Manitoba RST
operatingItems.description: Manitoba RST is reported to Manitoba Finance separately from GST.

items.name: New Brunswick Annual Return
items.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.
items.authority: Corporate Registry of New Brunswick (Service New Brunswick)

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in New Brunswick
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in New Brunswick
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside New Brunswick carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in New Brunswick and appoints an attorney for service where required.
extraProvincialItems.authority: Corporate Registry of New Brunswick (Service New Brunswick)

extraProvincialItems.name: New Brunswick Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: By the end of the month after the anniversary month of registration in New Brunswick
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside New Brunswick registered there (corporations from Nova Scotia need not register or file)
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the New Brunswick registry each year to stay in good standing.
extraProvincialItems.authority: Corporate Registry of New Brunswick (Service New Brunswick)

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (WorkSafeNB)
employerItems.rule: Form 100 annual payroll report by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in New Brunswick (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with WorkSafeNB when you hire in New Brunswick, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

items.name: Nova Scotia Annual Renewal
items.rule: During the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.
items.authority: Nova Scotia Registry of Joint Stock Companies

items.name: Nova Scotia Business Registration Renewal
items.rule: Annually, during the anniversary month of registration
items.applies: Sole proprietorships and partnerships registered in Nova Scotia
items.description: Registered business names and partnerships renew with the Registry of Joint Stock Companies each year.
items.authority: Nova Scotia Registry of Joint Stock Companies

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Nova Scotia
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Nova Scotia
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Nova Scotia carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in Nova Scotia and appoints an attorney for service where required.
extraProvincialItems.authority: Nova Scotia Registry of Joint Stock Companies

extraProvincialItems.name: Nova Scotia Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: During the anniversary month of registration in Nova Scotia
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Nova Scotia registered there (corporations from New Brunswick need not register or file)
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the Nova Scotia registry each year to stay in good standing.
extraProvincialItems.authority: Nova Scotia Registry of Joint Stock Companies

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia)
employerItems.rule: Payroll report and premium by the 15th of the month after each reporting period (monthly or quarterly, as assigned)
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Nova Scotia (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia when you hire in Nova Scotia, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.
employerItems.authority: Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia

items.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Annual Return
items.rule: Before the end of the anniversary month of incorporation
items.applies: Corporations incorporated in Newfoundland and Labrador
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.
items.authority: Newfoundland and Labrador Registry of Companies

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Newfoundland and Labrador
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Newfoundland and Labrador
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Newfoundland and Labrador carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in Newfoundland and Labrador and appoints an attorney for service where required.
extraProvincialItems.authority: Newfoundland and Labrador Registry of Companies

extraProvincialItems.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before the end of the anniversary month of registration
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Newfoundland and Labrador registered there
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the Newfoundland and Labrador registry each year to stay in good standing.
extraProvincialItems.authority: Newfoundland and Labrador Registry of Companies

employerItems.name: Health and Post-Secondary Education Tax (HAPSET)
employerItems.rule: Monthly return and payment by the 20th of the following month
employerItems.applies: Employers whose Newfoundland and Labrador payroll exceeds the $2 million exemption
employerItems.description: A 2% payroll tax on remuneration above the exemption.
employerItems.authority: Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Finance

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (WorkplaceNL)
employerItems.rule: Annual Employer Statement by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Newfoundland and Labrador (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with WorkplaceNL when you hire in Newfoundland and Labrador, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

items.name: PEI Annual Return
items.rule: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
items.applies: Corporations incorporated in Prince Edward Island
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office, directors and officers with the provincial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Prince Edward Island
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Prince Edward Island
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Prince Edward Island carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in Prince Edward Island and appoints an attorney for service where required.

extraProvincialItems.name: Prince Edward Island Extra-Provincial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: Renew the registration each year before the registration certificate expires (the anniversary of registration)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Prince Edward Island registered there
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-provincially registered corporations confirm their information with the Prince Edward Island registry each year to stay in good standing.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (Workers Compensation Board of PEI)
employerItems.rule: Annual registration renewal and payroll report by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Prince Edward Island (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with Workers Compensation Board of PEI when you hire in Prince Edward Island, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Provincial Registration in Quebec
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Quebec
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Quebec carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally or in another province) registers extra-provincially in Quebec and appoints an attorney for service where required.

employerItems.name: Quebec Source Deductions and Employer Contributions (Revenu Québec)
employerItems.rule: By the 15th of the month after the pay date (regular remitters)
employerItems.applies: Employers with employees working in Quebec
employerItems.description: Quebec income tax, QPP, QPIP and the employer's Health Services Fund contribution are remitted to Revenu Québec instead of (or as well as) the CRA.

employerItems.name: RL-1 Slips and RLZ-1.S Summary
employerItems.rule: Last day of February (for the previous calendar year)
employerItems.applies: Employers with employees working in Quebec
employerItems.description: The Quebec equivalent of T4 slips, with the summary reconciling source deductions, the Health Services Fund, CNT and WSDRF contributions.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (CNESST)
employerItems.rule: Annual statement of wages (déclaration des salaires) by 15 March
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Quebec (most industries)
employerItems.description: Register with CNESST when you hire in Quebec, pay premiums on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll.

operatingItems.name: Quebec Annual Updating Declaration and Registration Fee
operatingItems.rule: With the Quebec corporate tax return, within 6 months after financial year end (fee within 2 months); otherwise between 15 May and 15 November
operatingItems.description: Every enterprise registered with the Registraire des entreprises (including corporations from outside Quebec) confirms its information each year and pays the annual registration fee; corporations usually file it with their Quebec income tax return.

operatingItems.name: Quebec Annual Updating Declaration and Registration Fee
operatingItems.rule: Between 1 January and 15 June (fee by 30 April if filed with the income tax return)
operatingItems.applies: Sole proprietorships and partnerships registered in Quebec
operatingItems.description: Every enterprise registered with the Registraire des entreprises (including corporations from outside Quebec) confirms its information each year and pays the annual registration fee; corporations usually file it with their Quebec income tax return.

operatingItems.name: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17)
operatingItems.rule: Within 6 months after financial year end
operatingItems.applies: Corporations with an establishment in Quebec
operatingItems.description: Quebec collects its own corporate income tax, so a CO-17 is filed with Revenu Québec in addition to the federal T2.

operatingItems.applies: Businesses registered for QST (taxable supplies in Quebec over $30,000)
operatingItems.name: Quebec Sales Tax (QST) Return (annual filer)
operatingItems.rule: 3 months after financial year end (individuals with a 31 December year end: 15 June, with payment by 30 April)
operatingItems.description: QST is reported to Revenu Québec, together with GST in Quebec, for the same reporting period.

operatingItems.applies: Businesses registered for QST (taxable supplies in Quebec over $30,000)
operatingItems.name: Quebec Sales Tax (QST) Return (quarterly filer)
operatingItems.rule: 1 month after the end of each quarter of the financial year
operatingItems.description: QST is reported to Revenu Québec, together with GST in Quebec, for the same reporting period.

operatingItems.applies: Businesses registered for QST (taxable supplies in Quebec over $30,000)
operatingItems.name: Quebec Sales Tax (QST) Return (monthly filer)
operatingItems.rule: 1 month after the end of each month
operatingItems.description: QST is reported to Revenu Québec, together with GST in Quebec, for the same reporting period.

items.name: Yukon Annual Return
items.rule: By the last day of the month after the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office and directors with the territorial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Territorial Registration in Yukon
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Yukon
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Yukon carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally, in a province or another territory) registers as an extra-territorial corporation in Yukon.

extraProvincialItems.name: Yukon Extra-Territorial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: By the last day of the month after the anniversary month (we use the incorporation date; change it if your Yukon anniversary differs)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Yukon registered there
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-territorial corporations confirm their information with the Yukon registry each year to stay registered.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (Workers' Safety and Compensation Board (Yukon))
employerItems.rule: Employer payroll report by the last day of February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Yukon
employerItems.description: Register with the Workers' Safety and Compensation Board (Yukon) when you hire in Yukon, pay assessments on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll with an estimate for the coming year.

items.name: Northwest Territories Annual Return
items.rule: By the last day of the month after the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office and directors with the territorial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Territorial Registration in Northwest Territories
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Northwest Territories
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Northwest Territories carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally, in a province or another territory) registers as an extra-territorial corporation in Northwest Territories.

extraProvincialItems.name: Northwest Territories Extra-Territorial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: By the last day of the month after the anniversary month (we use the incorporation date; change it if your Northwest Territories anniversary differs)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Northwest Territories registered there
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-territorial corporations confirm their information with the Northwest Territories registry each year to stay registered.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (Workers' Safety and Compensation Commission (WSCC))
employerItems.rule: Annual Payroll Report by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Northwest Territories
employerItems.description: Register with the Workers' Safety and Compensation Commission (WSCC) when you hire in Northwest Territories, pay assessments on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll with an estimate for the coming year.

employerItems.name: Northwest Territories Payroll Tax Remittances
employerItems.rule: By the 20th of the month after each reporting period (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual or annual depending on payroll size)
employerItems.applies: Employers with employees working in Northwest Territories
employerItems.description: Employers deduct the territorial payroll tax (2% of employees' remuneration) and remit it on the schedule assigned at registration.
employerItems.authority: Government of the Northwest Territories, Department of Finance

employerItems.name: Northwest Territories Payroll Tax Annual Return
employerItems.rule: By the end of February of the following year
employerItems.applies: Employers with employees working in Northwest Territories
employerItems.description: The annual return reconciles the payroll tax deducted and remitted for the calendar year.
employerItems.authority: Government of the Northwest Territories, Department of Finance

items.name: Nunavut Annual Return
items.rule: By the last day of the month after the anniversary month of incorporation
items.description: Confirms the corporation's registered office and directors with the territorial registry each year; corporations that stop filing are eventually dissolved.

extraProvincialItems.name: Extra-Territorial Registration in Nunavut
extraProvincialItems.rule: Before (or promptly after) starting to carry on business in Nunavut
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Nunavut carrying on business there
extraProvincialItems.description: A corporation incorporated elsewhere (federally, in a province or another territory) registers as an extra-territorial corporation in Nunavut.

extraProvincialItems.name: Nunavut Extra-Territorial Annual Return
extraProvincialItems.rule: By the last day of the month after the anniversary month (we use the incorporation date; change it if your Nunavut anniversary differs)
extraProvincialItems.applies: Corporations from outside Nunavut registered there
extraProvincialItems.description: Extra-territorial corporations confirm their information with the Nunavut registry each year to stay registered.

employerItems.name: Workers' Compensation Reporting (Workers' Safety and Compensation Commission (WSCC))
employerItems.rule: Annual Payroll Report by 28 February
employerItems.applies: Employers with workers in Nunavut
employerItems.description: Register with the Workers' Safety and Compensation Commission (WSCC) when you hire in Nunavut, pay assessments on insurable earnings and report the year's payroll with an estimate for the coming year.

employerItems.name: Nunavut Payroll Tax Remittances
employerItems.rule: By the 20th of the month after each reporting period (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual or annual depending on payroll size)
employerItems.applies: Employers with employees working in Nunavut
employerItems.description: Employers deduct the territorial payroll tax (2% of employees' remuneration) and remit it on the schedule assigned at registration.
employerItems.authority: Government of Nunavut, Department of Finance

employerItems.name: Nunavut Payroll Tax Annual Return
employerItems.rule: By the end of February of the following year
employerItems.applies: Employers with employees working in Nunavut
employerItems.description: The annual return reconciles the payroll tax deducted and remitted for the calendar year.
employerItems.authority: Government of Nunavut, Department of Finance
